title: Who is who in The Last Lesson
back: M. Hamel (teacher, 40 years), Franz (narrator who changes), Hauser and the villagers (respect and regret), Wachter (the first hint).

title: The Last Lesson in six beats
back: Late → silence → announcement → blame → key to the prison → Vive La France! Six beats, one morning.

title: Language is the key to the prison
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="An enslaved people who keep their language stay free inside" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g opacity="0.9"><path d="M70.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M100.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M130.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M160.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M190.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M220.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M250.0,30 V160" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></g><g transform="translate(160,95) rotate(-20) scale(1.0)"><path d="M0,0 m-18,0 a18,18 0 1 0 36,0 a18,18 0 1 0 -36,0 M14,0 H90 V14 H78 V6 H66 V16 H54 V6 H18 Z M-18,0 a9,9 0 1 1 18,0 a9,9 0 1 1 -18,0" fill-rule="evenodd" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity="1" stroke="none"/></g><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">An enslaved people who keep their language stay free inside</text></svg>
back: M. Hamel's message: French is the clearest, most logical language; guard it. A conqueror attacks language to erase identity; keeping it keeps the way out. Examples: copies with France, Alsace; pigeons in German.

title: Tomorrow never came

back: Franz, the parents and M. Hamel himself all put learning off. The loss of the language makes everyone see the worth of what they neglected — the story's second theme after language.

title: The last two words
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Line to remember" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-size="11"><g><rect x="28" y="36" width="264" height="72" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/><path d="M50,108 L42,122 L64,108 Z" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="none"/><text x="160.0" y="79.0" text-anchor="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Vive La France!</text></g><text x="160" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.8" stroke="none">— chalked by M. Hamel, who could not speak</text><text x="160.0" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="none">Line to remember</text></svg>
back: At noon the Angelus and the Prussian trumpets sound; M. Hamel, pale and choked, writes the words as large as he can and dismisses the class with a gesture. His farewell is written, not spoken.
